items.concept: Touch is the first sense to fully develop in the womb — by 8 weeks, a fetus responds to light touch on its face. That's 13 weeks before hearing develops and 18 weeks before vision. The entire body is mapped by touch by week 16. Babies arrive as touch-sensing experts before they can hear a heartbeat clearly.
items.hook_text: First sense: not hearing, not sight

scene-1.text: The first sense to wire up in the womb isn't hearing — it's touch. By just 8 weeks, a fetus already flinches away from contact on its face.

scene-2.text: Hearing doesn't come online until week 18. Vision is even later. But touch? Touch is already mapping the entire body by week 16 — two months before a baby could survive outside the womb.

scene-3.text: This is why skin-to-skin contact right after birth is so powerful. Touch is the language babies speak first — before words, before faces, before sound.

items.concept: Newborns breathe 40-60 times per minute — triple the adult rate of 12-20 breaths. Their metabolism runs at three times adult speed to support rapid brain and organ development. First-time parents often panic, thinking something is wrong. Pediatricians call it 'normal newborn breathing' and watch for the opposite: slowness, not speed.

scene-1.text: If you watch a newborn breathe and count 60 breaths in a minute — that's completely normal. First-time parents call it terrifying. Pediatricians call it textbook.

scene-2.text: Adults breathe 12 to 20 times per minute. Newborns breathe 40 to 60. Their metabolism runs at triple speed — because their brain is doubling in size and every organ is building itself simultaneously.

scene-3.text: Doctors actually worry when newborns breathe slowly, not fast. The rapid rate is the engine of development. Every fast breath is fuel for the most intense growth window of a human life.

captions.youtube: Newborns breathe 40-60x per minute (adults: 12-20) — triple rate is normal, not a sign of distress. Their metabolism runs 3× speed to build brain and organs. #babyfacts

items.concept: Baby teeth begin forming at 6 weeks of pregnancy — over 8 months before a baby is born and 6+ months before a typical first tooth appears. All 20 primary teeth are fully formed, hidden under the gums, when a baby is born. The same process starts for permanent adult teeth in the second trimester. A toothless newborn is hiding a full set of teeth in their jaw.

scene-1.text: When a baby is born with that completely gummy smile — they're actually hiding 20 teeth. Every single primary tooth has already formed, waiting under the gums.

scene-2.text: Baby teeth start forming at 6 weeks of pregnancy. That's just 6 weeks after conception, 8 months before birth. By the second trimester, the permanent adult teeth are already beginning to form too.

scene-3.text: When that first tooth pokes through at 6 months, it didn't just grow — it was there the entire time. Every baby is born with a full hidden set, just waiting to arrive.

items.concept: FDIC insurance only covers $250,000 per depositor per bank. When Silicon Valley Bank failed in March 2023, 93% of its deposits were uninsured — over the $250K limit. The FDIC covered them anyway in an emergency ruling, but that protection is not guaranteed by law for future failures. Most Americans assume all bank deposits are fully protected — they are not.

scene-1.text: The FDIC guarantees your bank deposits — but only up to $250,000. Every dollar above that is at risk if your bank fails.

scene-2.text: When Silicon Valley Bank collapsed in 2023, 93% of its deposits were above the $250K limit. Uninsured. The FDIC covered them in an emergency decision — but that protection is not guaranteed by law for the next bank failure.

scene-3.text: Most Americans assume all bank deposits are fully protected. They are not. If you have more than $250K in one bank, you may want to understand what 'FDIC insured' actually means.

items.concept: In 1970, the median US home cost 3x the median household income. Today it costs 7.5x. That shift — a 150% increase in the price-to-income ratio — happened in one generation. In 1970, a family could buy a median home on 5 years of savings at 20%. Today it takes 12+ years. The housing rules your parents lived by no longer apply.

scene-1.text: In 1970, the median American home cost 3 times the median household income. Today it costs 7 and a half times. That shift happened in a single generation.

scene-2.text: In 1970, a family saving 20% of income could buy a median home in 5 years. Today? That same math takes over 12 years — and that assumes home prices don't keep climbing while you save.

scene-3.text: The housing rules your parents followed — save, buy, build equity — were written for a 3× income world. Nobody told you the rules changed.

items.concept: A median-wage worker contributing to Social Security for a full 40-year career pays in roughly $650,000 total (employer + employee combined). The average benefit payout is about $19,000 per year. Breakeven on contributions takes 34 years of benefits — most Americans never collect what they paid in. Social Security is legally not a savings account; the Supreme Court (Flemming v. Nestor, 1960) ruled Congress can change or cut benefits at any time.

scene-2.text: Breakeven on your contributions takes 34 years of collecting benefits. Most Americans never live long enough to collect what they paid in. And Social Security is not legally a savings account.

scene-3.text: In 1960, the Supreme Court ruled Congress can change or eliminate benefits at any time. Your contributions carry no legal guarantee of return. Most people don't know that.

items.concept: GPT-3 in 2020 could hold 4,000 tokens in context — roughly 3,000 words. GPT-4o today handles 128,000 tokens — an entire novel. That's a 32x expansion in 4 years. Gemini 1.5 Pro goes to 1 million tokens — 750,000 words, or about 10 novels. The practical limit of what an AI can 'read' and reason over in one session has grown 250x in under 5 years.

items.concept: Claude (Anthropic's AI) can read and process the entire Harry Potter series — all 7 books, 1.1 million words — in approximately 3 seconds. A fast human reader takes about 77 hours. The full collected works of Shakespeare (884,000 words) take Claude under 2 seconds. Modern LLMs don't just scan text faster — they extract meaning, relationships, and structure simultaneously. Reading speed is no longer a meaningful human competitive advantage.

scene-3.text: Reading speed used to be a human edge. The ability to absorb a document, analyze it, and pull out insights — AI does that 90,000 times faster. Reading is no longer a competitive skill.

items.concept: Insilico Medicine used AI to design a new drug molecule from scratch and advance it to Phase 2 clinical trials in 30 months. The traditional drug discovery timeline is 12-15 years. The AI identified the target, designed the molecule, and ran initial safety simulations before any human researcher touched a lab bench. In 2024, the first fully AI-designed drug entered Phase 3 trials. The pharmaceutical industry is about to face the same disruption as radiologists.

scene-1.text: Drug discovery normally takes 12 to 15 years. In 2021, Insilico Medicine used AI to design a new drug molecule from scratch and reach Phase 2 clinical trials in 30 months.

scene-2.text: The AI identified the disease target, designed the molecule, and ran initial safety simulations — before any human researcher touched a lab bench. In 2024, the first fully AI-designed drug entered Phase 3 trials.

scene-3.text: Pharmaceutical companies spend billions searching for molecules that fit disease proteins. AI screens millions of candidates in hours. The industry that gave us 12-year timelines is about to get the same disruption as radiologists.
